title: Diagnosing disappointment: six possible causes
objectives: Work through the six causes before agreeing “wrong time”.
Say which cause is usually least important for long-term money.
body_md:
When a client says “My fund isn't growing; did I invest at the wrong time?”, work through six possible causes before agreeing. Wrong measurement: are we reading absolute return over a short period, or a SIP's total instead of XIRR? Wrong horizon: how long has it been, and how long is it meant for? Wrong expectation: what return did the client expect, and why? Market phase: did the whole market or category fall? Wrong fund: has the fund lagged its benchmark and category over 3–5 years? Wrong time: was a large lump sum invested just before a fall, for a short horizon? Often the answer is a combination, and “wrong time” is usually the least important cause for long-term money.

| Possible cause | Question to check | What it looks like | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wrong measurement | Are we reading absolute return over a short period, or a SIP's total instead of XIRR? | "Only 8% in 2 years" on a SIP | Recalculate with XIRR (Module 10) |
| Wrong horizon | How long has it been, and how long is it meant for? | Equity held for 1–2 years | Reset expectations; equity needs 5+ years |
| Wrong expectation | What return did the client expect, and why? | Expected last year's 40% to repeat | Show long-term, realistic ranges |
| Market phase | Did the whole market or category fall? | Fund and benchmark both down | Normal volatility; stay the course if the horizon allows |
| Wrong fund | Has the fund lagged its benchmark and category over 3–5 years? | Fund down 10%, benchmark up 5% | Review the fund (Module 1 review checklist) |
| Wrong time | Was a large lump sum invested just before a fall, for a short horizon? | Lump sum at a peak, money needed in 2 years | Review the asset mix for the goal date; no panic selling |

> **Investor takeaway:** Before blaming the timing, check the measure, the horizon, the expectation and the fund.
example: “Only 8% in 2 years” on a SIP: recalculate with XIRR before judging — the statement total is not the yearly return.
say: Check measure, horizon, expectation and fund before blaming timing.
“Wrong time” is usually least important for long-term money.
never: A fund down 10% while its benchmark is up 5% is a market-wide fall.

check.q: A client’s fund fell 18% while its benchmark fell 20% over the same period. What is the most likely cause?
check.why: A market-wide fall. The fund did slightly better than its benchmark; the whole market fell.

check.q: A client's fund fell 12% in a year. What should you do first?
o: Conclude the investment was a mistake
Diagnose the cause: measure, horizon, expectation, market, fund
check.why: Falls are a normal feature of equity; diagnose the cause first.

check.q: A fund fell 10% while its benchmark fell 11%. What does that suggest?
o: A market-wide fall — the fund did slightly better than its benchmark
check.why: Fund and benchmark both down: normal volatility; stay the course if the horizon allows.
